record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Complete solvability for regular orthodox classes
record.original_question: Determine whether the following classes are completely solvable: (1) finite regular orthodox semigroups; and (2) finite regular semigroups whose idempotents belong to a given variety of idempotent semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.4. (S.I. Kublanovsky)

     (1) Is the class of finite regular orthodox semigroups completely solvable?
     (2) The same question for the class of finite regular semigroups, whose idempotents belong to
         a given variety of idempotent semigroups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A class K of finite semigroups is said to be completely solvable if there exists an algorithm that, given a finite semigroup S (presented, say, by its multiplication table), decides whether S belongs to K, and moreover decides membership in K for every finitely generated subsemigroup-defining problem associated with K (i.e., the membership problem for K is decidable in a uniform algorithmic sense).

Recall the following definitions:
- A semigroup S is regular if for every a ∈ S there exists x ∈ S with a x a = a.
- An element e ∈ S is idempotent if e² = e; the set of idempotents of S is denoted E(S).
- A regular semigroup S is orthodox if E(S) is a subsemigroup of S (equivalently, the product of any two idempotents of S is again idempotent).
- A variety of idempotent semigroups (band variety) is a class of semigroups satisfying e² = e together with some additional set of identities, closed under taking subsemigroups, homomorphic images, and direct products.

Determine whether each of the following classes of finite semigroups is completely solvable:

(1) The class of all finite regular orthodox semigroups.

(2) For a fixed variety V of idempotent semigroups, the class of all finite regular semigroups S such that the band E(S) (with the multiplication inherited from S) belongs to V.
